timeline_reviews.summary: Main trajectory transport ledger contained no semantic events but accounted for the outer single-agent conversation stream.
Serial agent probed CLI and markdown behavior, then implemented a manual CLI parser plus runtime wrapper that executes the reference executable, verified representative cases, and finalized.

parallel.requirements: Recognized ESM .mjs output, manual argv parsing, local modules, no npm dependencies, no Python command, and byte-for-byte parity with Python-Markdown behavior.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent kept final /output ownership while delegating behavior probing to markdown and argparse children; the markdown child further delegated CLI and highlight probes and then began a separate implementation.
parallel.implementation: Parent wrote a local Markdown parser/highlighter stack plus CLI parser and pipeline in /output, covering sample cases, headings, code spans, TOC IDs, tables, and codehilite approximations.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The deliverable tree came from the parent under /output, while the markdown child's separate /workspace/output implementation was not promoted or reconciled before final response.
parallel.verification: Parent compared all four prompt samples and targeted TOC and CLI edge cases against the executable; official evaluation later passed only 15 of 70 samples.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The local Markdown clone remained incomplete for hidden Python-Markdown behavior, and the active markdown child was interrupted before finalizing its separate work.

serial.requirements: Recognized ESM output, manual argv parsing, exact output matching, and no npm dependencies, but treated the reference executable as a runtime implementation mechanism.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single agent owned probing, implementation, verification, and delivery without delegation; it split code into CLI parser/spec/messages and runtime executable modules.
serial.implementation: Implemented argv parsing locally but made the transformation path call /workspace/dataset/test19_executable through Node child_process instead of reimplementing Markdown behavior in JS.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Delivered a coherent /output tree with test19.mjs and local CLI/runtime modules; there were no child artifacts to merge or reconcile.
serial.verification: Checked representative successful cases and parser errors against the executable, but those checks used the same reference executable that the solution depended on at runtime.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial artifact was not a standalone migration and failed all official samples, likely because the runtime depended on the dataset executable rather than implementing the transformation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel aimed to satisfy standalone Node ESM, manual argv parsing, and local markdown modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized parsing and ESM requirements but retained a runtime dependency on the reference executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel attempted a real JS Markdown reimplementation; serial optimized for exact oracle output by calling the oracle at runtime, violating the standalone migration intent.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split behavior probing across markdown and argparse children while the parent owned final implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all probing, implementation, and verification in one thread with no subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained broader behavior probing but introduced a child lifecycle to manage; serial avoided coordination risk but chose a simpler invalid wrapper design.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent received concrete argparse findings and listed child state, but the markdown child's own final return was never delivered after interruption.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used its own probes directly and had no handoff boundary between investigator and implementer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel run had useful child information, but one markdown-result boundary remained unfinished; the serial run's context was local and continuous.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote actual Markdown conversion modules, including inline parsing, escaping, tables, TOC, code highlighting, a phase pipeline, and test19.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote CLI parser modules and a runtime module that invokes the reference executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel tried to implement the transformation logic; serial implemented mostly argument validation and delegated the core transformation externally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel unsuccessfully tried a short wait, inspected agent status, interrupted the still-running markdown child, and then finalized.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results; it completed local work and updated the plan before final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost a child result lifecycle through explicit interruption, while serial's single-thread lifecycle closed without a join boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent's final tree was in /output; the markdown child wrote a separate /workspace/output tree that was not part of the copied artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one coherent /output tree consisting of CLI parser modules, runtime executable wrapper, and entry file.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an unintegrated side implementation from a child, but no proven overwrite of the parent's delivered files; serial had no shared-state merge problem.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel reported byte-for-byte matches on the four prompt samples and targeted TOC/CLI cases, but official evaluation passed only 15/70.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial compared representative runs against the executable and reported parser checks, but official evaluation passed 0/70.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's checks validated a partial local clone; serial's checks mainly validated that it could call the oracle, which did not translate to an accepted standalone solution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent 475.792 agent seconds with five subagents, ended without timeout, and closed after interrupting a still-running child.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial spent 361.882 agent seconds, had no subagents, ended without timeout, and closed after local verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more budget and concurrency overhead but did not exhaust the run; the meaningful closure difference is the interrupted child, not raw duration.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The completed official status records make this a both_fail pair: parallel passed 15/70 and serial passed 0/70. The score gap is explained by different implementation strategies, not by a pass/fail discordance: parallel attempted a local Markdown clone and covered the supplied samples and some probes, while serial made the core runtime call the reference executable and therefore did not deliver a standalone JS migration. The retained parallel coordination issue is adverse because an active markdown child was interrupted before final return, but it does not explain a discordant official outcome because neither solution passed.
parallel_contributors: Parallel built local Markdown modules and therefore achieved partial official coverage.
Parallel interrupted the markdown-behavior child before its final result, leaving some in-progress probing/implementation work unused.
serial_contributors: Serial kept all work local and avoided child lifecycle risk.
Serial failed as a standalone migration by forwarding the transformation to /workspace/dataset/test19_executable at runtime.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial's executable-wrapper runtime is an ordinary implementation defect, not a concurrency pattern.
Parallel's partial Markdown clone missed hidden Python-Markdown behavior despite matching visible probes.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

The record does not show incompatible child reports that remained unadjudicated at the parent decision point.

There was no replacement or retry of the same delegated work without inherited checkpoint state.

candidates.reason: The parent explicitly interrupted an active markdown-behavior child before that child finalized its result or in-progress implementation work.
candidates.realized_consequence: The markdown-behavior child's active renderer/probing work was left without a final handoff, and the parent closed with only its own partial clone.
candidates.near_match_reason: The same chain starts with an explicit interrupt; any missing takeover is downstream and not a distinct failure-propagation episode.

candidates.reason: No complete promotable child candidate existed before closure; the child modules were unfinished and then interrupted.
No child implementation was merged after integrated verification; the child implementation was not joined at all before finalization.
The markdown child had not completed a retrievable implementation before interruption, so the direct lifecycle boundary is early termination.
No verifier child completed a concrete finding that remained trapped; the relevant markdown child was interrupted before its own final return.
The interrupted markdown child is already captured by Early Child Termination; no separate failed child episode required a distinct takeover decision.
Completed argparse and nested probe findings were visible and not shown to be ignored at a contrary parent decision point.
The parent did not wait blindly until timeout; it listed child state and explicitly interrupted the remaining child.
Parent and child wrote different implementation trees, but no competing delivered design required reconciliation in the final artifact.
There is no evidence that two live agents edited the same source file and observed or reconciled a concurrent change.
No agent replaced or wholesale rewrote non-entry source produced or actively owned by another agent.
No live agent overwrote the submitted entry file or required deliverable while another agent owned it.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current final outputs or invalidated another final tree.
The child wrote a separate /workspace/output tree, but no unstable shared-workspace state or provenance problem affected the delivered /output artifact.
No generated artifact, cache, fixture, process, or temporary file from one concurrent actor was consumed by another as stable input.
